text: A quasi-category (the Joyal-Lurie model of an $(\infty,1)$-category) is defined as a simplicial set satisfying which condition?
choices: Every outer horn ($\Lambda^n_0$ or $\Lambda^n_n$) admits a filler
Every map from the boundary $\partial\Delta^n$ extends to $\Delta^n$
Every inner horn $\Lambda^n_k$ with $0<k<n$ admits a filler $\Delta^n\to\mathcal{C}$
Every simplex above dimension $1$ is degenerate
explanation: The chapter defines a quasi-category by the inner horn filling condition: for $0<k<n$, every inner horn $\Lambda^n_k\to\mathcal{C}$ has a filler $\Delta^n\to\mathcal{C}$, so compositions exist but only up to homotopy. Filling the outer horns ($k=0,n$) is the stronger condition defining an $\infty$-groupoid; extending every boundary or forcing degeneracy are unrelated to the definition.
